title: Seller Property Disclosure Form
description: Arkansas Code §18-44-104 requires sellers of residential real property (1-4 units) to provide a completed property disclosure form to buyers before acceptance of the purchase offer. The disclosure covers structural, mechanical, environmental, and known defects. Certain transfers (foreclosures, estates, new construction) are exempt under §18-44-103.

required_actions.note: Disclosure must be provided before acceptance of the purchase contract. Buyer may rescind within 5 days of receipt if not timely provided.

title: Agency Relationship Disclosure
description: Arkansas Code §17-42-502 requires licensees to provide written disclosure of agency relationships at the first substantive contact with each party. Arkansas permits dual agency with written informed consent. Transaction licensees (facilitators) are also recognized when no agency relationship exists.

required_actions.note: Must be provided at first substantive contact. Dual agency requires written consent of both parties.

title: Title Company or Attorney Closing
description: Arkansas allows closings through title companies or attorneys. Attorney presence is not required by statute, and title companies may handle closings. Title insurance is standard practice for residential transactions.

required_actions.note: Both title companies and attorneys may conduct closings. Attorney not required.

title: Flood Zone and Water Damage Disclosure
description: Arkansas's property disclosure form (§18-44-104) includes specific questions about prior flood damage, whether the property is in a FEMA-designated flood zone, and whether flood insurance has been required or maintained. Sellers must disclose known flooding history and current flood zone status.

required_actions.note: Flood history and flood zone status must be disclosed on the statutory property disclosure form.
Lenders require flood insurance for properties in FEMA SFHA zones.

title: Real Estate Advertising Requirements
description: Arkansas Real Estate Commission regulations require that all real estate advertising include the licensed name of the brokerage firm. Licensees may not advertise property without the broker's authorization. Advertising must not be misleading or deceptive, and team names must include the brokerage name.

required_actions.note: All advertising must include the licensed brokerage name. Team advertising must also include brokerage name.
